extent.title: Area later enclosed by the Aurelian Walls (AD 271-275)
extent.note: The outer limit of the zoning, taken from the surviving wall ways in OpenStreetMap and today's east bank of the Tiber, with the lost Trastevere stretch drawn through the site of Porta Aurelia. The walls did not exist in AD 100 and are not drawn; the built-up area then spilled past this line in places.

zones.title: Tiber
zones.note: Today's channel (OpenStreetMap), standing in for the ancient river, which was wider and had no embankments (begun 1876). Inside the city only.

zones.title: Capitoline, Forum Romanum, Palatine, Colosseum valley and Circus Maximus
zones.note: Temples, basilicas, imperial fora (Caesar, Augustus, the Templum Pacis, Nerva's forum of AD 97), the palaces on the Palatine, the Flavian amphitheatre (AD 80) and the Circus Maximus, around Pleiades points for each. The Velabrum between the Capitoline and the Palatine is left to housing. The saddle where Trajan's Forum was built from about AD 106 is left out of this zone and falls to housing; what stood there at AD 100 is uncertain. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Oppian: Baths of Titus and the Domus Aurea pavilion
zones.note: The Baths of Titus (AD 80) and the surviving Oppian wing of Nero's Domus Aurea, which burned in AD 104 and lay under the Baths of Trajan by 109. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Caelian: Temple of the Deified Claudius
zones.note: The terrace of the Temple of Claudius, completed by Vespasian. Placed by the Regio II record; its size here is a round figure. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Forum Holitorium, Theatre of Marcellus and the Circus Flaminius porticoes
zones.note: The vegetable market and its temples, the Theatre of Marcellus (13 BC), the Porticus Octaviae and the Circus Flaminius, a public square ringed by temples and porticoes. The circus's exact line is disputed; the outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Central Campus Martius: Pantheon, Saepta, Baths of Agrippa, Stadium of Domitian, Theatre of Pompey
zones.note: Public buildings packed close: Agrippa's Pantheon and baths, the Saepta Julia, the temples of the Largo Argentina, Pompey's theatre and portico, and Domitian's stadium and odeum (after AD 86). The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Northern Campus Martius: Mausoleum of Augustus, Ara Pacis and the sundial
zones.note: Augustus's mausoleum and its park, the Ara Pacis (9 BC) and the Horologium, placed from their Pleiades points. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Castra Praetoria (camp of the Praetorian Guard)
zones.note: The walled camp built under Tiberius (AD 23) on the plateau beyond the Viminal, later taken into the Aurelian circuit. Placed as a rectangle of about 440 by 380 m; the outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Tiber Island: sanctuary of Aesculapius
zones.note: The island and its sanctuary (temple of Aesculapius, 291 BC; temple of Faunus, 196 BC). The island is today's outline; its ancient shore is not traced, so the edge is a guess.

zones.title: Emporium, Porticus Aemilia and the horrea below the Aventine
zones.note: The river port on the plain south of the Aventine: the Emporium quay (Pleiades point), the Porticus Aemilia warehouse (193 BC) and the horrea (Galbana, Lolliana and others) between it and the hill, with the riverside strip north to the Forum Boarium. The amphora dump of Monte Testaccio was growing here; it is not modelled. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Trastevere riverfront
zones.note: A band about 100 m deep along the west bank south of the island, where landing places and storehouses for the river traffic are likely but not mapped. Its depth and extent are a guess.

zones.title: Pincian (Collis Hortorum): Horti Luculliani, Sallustiani and others
zones.note: The hill of gardens: the Horti Luculliani above the Campus and the imperial Horti Sallustiani in the valley towards the Quirinal, placed by their Pleiades points. Mostly gardens, pavilions and a few great houses. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Esquiline: Horti Maecenatis and Lamiani
zones.note: The gardens laid out over the old Esquiline cemetery beyond the Servian agger (Maecenas's, then imperial; the Lamian gardens beside them), placed by their Pleiades points. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Esquiline and Viminal plateau towards the later wall
zones.note: The outer plateau between the Castra Praetoria and the aqueduct junction near the later Porta Maggiore. Suburban gardens and villas are likely; nothing specific is mapped here. The extent is a guess.

zones.title: Eastern Caelian: great houses and gardens
zones.note: The eastern Caelian, towards the later Lateran, was a quarter of large houses with gardens (the house of the Laterani among them). The extent and the share of garden are guesses.

zones.title: Via Appia beyond Porta Capena: tombs, gardens and villas
zones.note: Outside the Servian gate the Appian Way was lined with tombs (the Scipios' among them) between gardens and villas, later enclosed by the Aurelian wall. Character and extent are a guess.

zones.title: Janiculum slopes
zones.note: The slope up to the Janiculum within the later wall, likely villas and gardens above the Trastevere streets (a late-republican villa stood by the river at the Farnesina). The extent is a guess.

zones.title: Northern Campus Martius: open ground towards the Via Flaminia
zones.note: North and west of the Mausoleum, towards where the Via Flaminia left the city. Strabo describes the Campus as open ground for exercise and games; by AD 100 building had spread north along the Via Lata, so how much stayed open here is a guess.

zones.title: Dense housing: the east bank (Subura, Velabrum, Via Lata, Quirinal, Viminal, Esquiline, Caelian, Aventine)
zones.note: Everything inside the city not assigned to another zone. Dense blocks of flats over shops are attested in the Subura, the Argiletum and the Velabrum and along the Via Lata; the Aventine and Caelian mixed flats with large houses. The zone is the remainder of the others, so its edges are theirs: approximate. Dated from the rebuilding after the fire of AD 64.

zones.title: Housing: Trastevere (Regio XIV)
zones.note: Across the river: workshops, flats and immigrant communities on the flat ground below the Janiculum, generally less dense than the east-bank core. The zone is the remainder of the others, so its edges are theirs: approximate. Dated from the rebuilding after the fire of AD 64.
